$comment: GENERATED by the Simple Icons post-process — do not edit by hand.
whyTheseAreNotTheDrawnSet: The drawn set is stroked: 18-unit grid, 1-unit stroke, no fill, four closed keylines. Simple Icons are FILLED silhouettes, so they satisfy none of that and cannot be converted to it — a fill cannot be turned into a 1-unit stroke by any transform. They live in the .platform fence, with their own origin and their own rule, exactly as assets/icons/README.md requires.
postProcess: rescaled from 24 to the round keyline 13 in an 18-unit box
ink coverage measured by rasterising at 72px and summing alpha — filled area is the right analogue of the drawn set's path length
per-icon scale corrected by sqrt(median/coverage), since area scales as the square
clamped to 0.82-1.18 so an intrinsically light silhouette is not blown past its keyline to fake weight, nor a dense one shrunk into illegibility
flattened to one tone: currentColor for inline use, #7f7f79 for background-image

linkedin.title: LinkedIn
linkedin.note: clamped at 0.871 — a heavy silhouette, and the keyline is the harder constraint

trademark: CC0 covers the FILE, not the brand. The marks stay unmodified beyond this flattening, always sit beside their own name, and never imply endorsement.

twbs/icons.why: simple-icons does not carry LinkedIn — the owner had the mark removed. Bootstrap Icons is MIT and ships brand glyphs, so the mark comes from there through the identical post-process and into the identical fence.
